summary.title: Gluon Radiation of an Expanding Color Skyrmion in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
summary.executive_summary: This paper investigates the gluon radiation emitted by an expanding color skyrmion within a quark-gluon plasma (QGP) using a semiclassical approach. The study addresses the hydrodynamic stage of deconfined hot QCD matter, specifically modeling the transport of color charges via a nonlinear sigma model. The author derives the nonabelian current corresponding to a time-dependent, expanding soliton solution, which mimics the expanding nature of the RHIC fireball. By calculating the semiclassical amplitude for gluon emission from this classical current, the paper determines the density of states and the energy spectrum of the radiation. The results reveal a distinct spectral pattern: a fast fall-off in the ultraviolet (UV) region, a smooth peak in the intermediate energy range, and a long tail in the infrared (IR) region. The IR behavior is characterized by a $1/\sqrt{k}$ dependence, which contrasts with the $1/k$ behavior found in previous literature where the medium size was assumed to be infinite. This difference is attributed to the finite soliton size $R_0$ in the current model. The work also discusses the hierarchy between medium-induced gluon radiation (jet quenching) and radiation from the medium itself, noting that the characteristic momentum of the latter is significantly smaller. The study suggests that this hydrodynamic approach could provide insights into the eccentricity of elliptic flow in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, offering a new avenue for understanding the physical mechanisms underlying particle production spectra.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper investigates the gluon radiation emitted by an expanding color skyrmion within a quark-gluon plasma (QGP) using a semiclassical approach. The study addresses the hydrodynamic stage of deconfined hot QCD matter, specifically modeling the transport of color charges via a nonlinear sigma model. The author derives the nonabelian current corresponding to a time-dependent, expanding soliton solution, which mimics the expanding nature of the RHIC fireball. By calculating the semiclassical amplitude for gluon emission from this classical current, the paper determines the density of states and the energy spectrum of the radiation. The results reveal a distinct spectral pattern: a fast fall-off in the ultraviolet (UV) region, a smooth peak in the intermediate energy range, and a long tail in the infrared (IR) region. The IR behavior is characterized by a $1/\sqrt{k}$ dependence, which contrasts with the $1/k$ behavior found in previous literature where the medium size was assumed to be infinite. This difference is attributed to the finite soliton size $R_0$ in the current model. The work also discusses the hierarchy between medium-induced gluon radiation (jet quenching) and radiation from the medium itself, noting that the characteristic momentum of the latter is significantly smaller. The study suggests that this hydrodynamic approach could provide insights into the eccentricity of elliptic flow in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, offering a new avenue for understanding the physical mechanisms underlying particle production spectra.

Research Context
The study addresses gluon radiation during the hydrodynamic stage of deconfined hot QCD matter. Medium-induced gluon radiation has been explored in the context of jet quenching. Spatially extended nuclear matter affects fragmentation and hadronization of hard partons. Gluon radiation is also considered in the context of gluon density saturation. The time evolution of the RHIC fireball influences observable particle production spectra. The resulting state of matter is modeled as a relativistic fluid. Generalized fluid mechanics characterizes the long-distance physics of color charge transport. A type of single skyrmion solutions in color fluid was discovered. A time-dependent skyrmion expands in time, matching the expanding fireball nature. The pattern of gluon radiation is an important character of this color skyrmion.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is the calculation of the gluon radiation spectrum for an expanding color skyrmion. The hypothesis is that the radiation can be calculated using a semiclassical approach. It is predicted that there is a fast fall-off in the UV side of the spectrum. A smooth peak is predicted to dominate the intermediate energy region. A long tail is predicted as the characteristic feature in the IR region. The study aims to compare these results with those in existing literatures. The model assumes a hierarchy between partonic coupling and effective coupling. Gluon self-interaction is omitted to work with a free parton picture. The lowest order semiclassical amplitude is derived from the interaction of current and field. The spatial Fourier transformation is completed analytically to simplify the amplitude.

Methodological Details
The transport of color charges is modeled by a nonlinear sigma model. The configuration of the fluid is described by a group element field U. The velocity field is defined using the trace of the group element derivative. The abelian charge current is conjugate to the velocity. The fluid takes values in an SU(2) group. The equation of state is approximated by radiation-like behavior at high temperature. The free energy density is derived by integrating the energy and pressure densities. Expanding soliton solutions are studied via variational and collective coordinate methods. The soliton size R(t) follows a specific time-dependent expansion law. The approximation is valid provided the temporal scale is much smaller than the spatial scale. A small parameter lambda is defined as the ratio of temporal to spatial scales. The hedgehog ansatz is specified for the soliton solution. The stereographic map is used to define the angle phi. The nonabelian current is derived from the abelian current via the Eckart factorization. The current is expressed in terms of the velocity and the soliton orientation. Only the lowest mode of the multipole expansion is considered in this letter. The spherically symmetric part of the current is contained in the third component. The interaction between the skyrmion and hard partons is considered. The gauge coupling becomes the coupling between a classical current and a free quantum field. The lowest order semiclassical amplitude is calculated using the Fock vacuum and one-gluon state. The gluon factor is given by the wave function with color and helicity parts. The spatial Fourier transformation is completed analytically. The time integral is evaluated using the specific form of R(t). The on-shell condition is applied to relate frequency and momentum. The radiation spectrum is given by the energy radiated over the entire time of expansion. The number distribution is calculated by summing over colors and helicities. The density of states is derived in a spherically symmetric setting. Numerical results are calculated for specific values of lambda.

Procedures And Architectures
The Lagrangian density includes terms for charge current, free energy, and gauge coupling. The velocity field is defined as the trace of the group element derivative. The energy and pressure densities are given by the ideal fluid formula. The nonabelian charge density is related to the abelian current by the Eckart factor. The free energy density is obtained by integrating the equation of state. The expanding soliton solution is given by a specific time-dependent radius function. The hedgehog ansatz is used to specify the group element field. The stereographic map defines the sine and cosine of the angle phi. The nonabelian current is derived using the equation of motion. The current has a natural form of a multipole expansion. The spherically symmetric part of the current is isolated. The semiclassical amplitude is given by the integral of the current and field. The gluon factor is the wave function of the one-gluon state. The spatial Fourier transformation is completed analytically. The time integral is evaluated using the expansion law of the soliton. The on-shell condition is used to define the parameter kappa. The final amplitude is expressed in terms of a function f_M. The number distribution is calculated by summing the squared amplitude. The density of states is derived for a spherically symmetric setting. The energy spectrum is calculated as the derivative of energy with respect to k. The numerical results are plotted for different values of lambda.

Key Results
The density of states is proportional to alpha, R0, lambda squared, and kappa to the power of negative one-half. The energy spectrum is proportional to alpha, lambda squared, kappa to the power of one-half, and the squared amplitude. The numerical results are shown for lambda equal to 1/15, 2/15, and 1/5. There is a fast fall-off in the UV side of the spectrum. A smooth peak dominates the intermediate energy region. A long tail is the characteristic feature in the IR region. The asymptotic behavior of the number density in small k is proportional to 1 over square root of k. This differs from the 1/k form found in previous literature. The difference is due to the finite medium size characterized by the soliton size R0. The IR behavior in this case is softer than in the infinite medium case. The characteristic momentum in this case is 1 over R0. The medium-induced gluon radiation frequency is significantly larger than the characteristic momentum. There is a hierarchy between the medium-induced spectrum and the medium radiation spectrum.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The pattern of gluon radiation is an important character of the color skyrmion. The hydrodynamic approach opens up possibilities to address the eccentricity of elliptic flow. This can be done intrinsically by considering the nonabelian color current. It can also be done exogenously by considering the gluon radiation patterns. Understanding the radiation pattern is important for determining physical mechanisms. The study provides a new perspective on the hydrodynamic stage of QGP evolution. The finite size of the medium affects the IR behavior of the radiation. The results suggest a distinct spectral shape compared to infinite medium approximations. The work highlights the importance of the soliton size in determining the radiation spectrum. Future work will explore the connection to elliptic flow.

Contradictions And Limitations
The study only considers the effect of the lowest mode of the multipole expansion. The effects of higher polarization will be considered elsewhere. The approximation is valid provided the temporal scale is much smaller than the spatial scale. Gluon self-interaction is omitted in the free parton picture. The medium size is characterized by the soliton size R0, unlike previous infinite medium models. The origin of the two scales R0 and tau is not understood from a fundamental level. The study is a letter, so some details may be omitted. The numerical results are only shown for specific values of lambda. The comparison with jet quenching is qualitative regarding the hierarchy of scales. The application to elliptic flow is proposed for future work, not demonstrated here.

Claims
The gluon radiation spectrum from an expanding color skyrmion has a distinct shape with a UV fall-off, intermediate peak, and IR tail. The spectrum shows a fast fall-off in the UV side. A smooth peak dominates the intermediate energy. A long tail is the characteristic feature in the IR. The IR behavior is softer than the 1/k form in previous literature. This pattern is an important character of the color skyrmion.
The finite size of the medium leads to a softer IR behavior compared to infinite medium models. The asymptotic number density is proportional to 1 over square root of k. The medium size is characterized by the soliton size R0. Previous literature found a 1/k form for infinite medium size. The IR behavior in this case is softer.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The study considers only the lowest mode of the multipole expansion. Higher polarization effects are not included in this letter. The approximation relies on the small parameter lambda. The free parton picture omits gluon self-interaction.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows the density of states and energy spectrum for different lambda values. Figure 2 shows the behavior of n over 1 over square root of kappa in small k.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the calculation of the gluon radiation spectrum for an expanding color skyrmion. 2. The strongest evidence is the distinct spectral shape with a UV fall-off, intermediate peak, and IR tail. 3. The future path is to address the eccentricity of elliptic flow using this hydrodynamic approach.
